properties.name: Piedmont
properties.desc: Home of Nebbiolo. Barolo and Barbaresco are Italy's most structured and age-worthy reds. Also famous for Barbera, Dolcetto and sparkling Moscato.

properties.name: Valle d'Aosta
properties.desc: Tiny alpine region with distinctive local varieties and high-altitude wines.

properties.name: Liguria
properties.desc: Dramatic terraced vineyards on the coast. Fresh Vermentino/Pigato whites and light Rossese reds.

properties.name: Lombardy
properties.desc: Home of Franciacorta, Italy's top traditional-method sparkling wine, plus alpine Nebbiolo from Valtellina.

properties.name: Trentino-Alto Adige
properties.desc: Alpine precision. Crisp whites, elegant Pinot Nero and distinctive Lagrein and Schiava from high-altitude vineyards.

properties.name: Veneto
properties.desc: Italy's volume leader and home of Prosecco, rich Amarone and crisp Soave. Extremely diverse styles from sparkling to powerful dried-grape reds.

properties.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
properties.desc: Italy's white-wine powerhouse. Precise, mineral whites from Collio and Colli Orientali, plus characterful local reds.

properties.name: Emilia-Romagna
properties.desc: Famous for Lambrusco (now often dry and serious) and solid Sangiovese from Romagna.

properties.name: Marche
properties.desc: Verdicchio produces some of Italy's finest white wines — mineral, age-worthy and still under-appreciated.

properties.name: Tuscany
properties.desc: Sangiovese heartland. Chianti Classico, Brunello and the Super Tuscans define Italian red wine for many drinkers worldwide.

properties.name: Umbria
properties.desc: Home of the powerful, tannic Sagrantino di Montefalco and classic Orvieto whites.

properties.name: Lazio
properties.desc: Historic white-wine region around Rome, plus emerging quality reds from Cesanese.

properties.name: Campania
properties.desc: Volcanic soils and ancient varieties. Taurasi (the 'Barolo of the South'), Fiano and Greco produce some of Italy's finest reds and whites.

properties.name: Abruzzo
properties.desc: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is one of Italy's great value reds — juicy, structured and widely available.

properties.name: Molise
properties.desc: Small region with solid Montepulciano and the local Tintilia grape.

properties.name: Puglia
properties.desc: Sunny southern reds. Powerful Primitivo and Negroamaro, increasingly refined and value-driven.

properties.name: Basilicata
properties.desc: Aglianico del Vulture — volcanic soils and one of southern Italy's greatest red grapes.

properties.name: Calabria
properties.desc: Cirò and other coastal reds from Gaglioppo; still emerging on the international scene.

properties.name: Sicily
properties.desc: Volcanic Etna reds and whites are among Italy's most exciting wines. Nero d'Avola and ancient Marsala complete the picture.

properties.name: Sardinia
properties.desc: Island character. Robust Cannonau (Grenache) and aromatic Vermentino thrive in the Mediterranean climate.
